core_obligations: Reduce to cohomology sheaves (proof lines 6381-6382): K -> Rf_*f^*K is an isomorphism if and only if it is an isomorphism on all cohomology sheaves H^j.
Use truncation and flatness (proof line 6383): H^j(Rf_*f^*K) = H^j(Rf_*tau_{<= j}f^*K) = H^j(Rf_*f^*tau_{<= j}K), so one may assume K is bounded.

Place K in the subcategory D' (proof lines 6384-6387): hypothesis (3) puts the cohomology sheaves in D', and boundedness plus stability of D' under distinguished triangles puts K itself in D', which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Check the map on cohomology sheaves instead of on the objects.
Use truncation and flatness to reduce to a bounded K.
Hypothesis (3) puts each cohomology sheaf in the downstairs subcategory D'.
Boundedness and stability under triangles put K in D'.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the dual criterion of its upstairs companion: for a flat morphism of ringed topoi and a bounded below K, if each H^q(K) satisfies H^q(K) -> Rf_*f^*H^q(K) then K -> Rf_*f^*K is an isomorphism (statement lines 6367-6378). The proof passes to cohomology sheaves and uses the truncation identities H^j(Rf_*f^*K) = H^j(Rf_*tau_{<= j}f^*K) = H^j(Rf_*f^*tau_{<= j}K) to reduce to a bounded K, after which hypothesis (3) places the cohomology sheaves in the subcategory D' of the downstairs lemma and boundedness plus stability under triangles places K there (proof lines 6381-6387). The non-formal content is the truncation computation that makes the reduction legitimate. The claim is H2: one reduction of the same shape as its companion, with its own truncation identity.
